clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 2. The interpreter instruction tables ... handlers of ADD, MUL, SUB, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, ADDMOD, MULMOD, EXP, SIGNEXTEND, LT, GT, SLT, SGT, EQ, ISZERO, AND, OR, XOR, NOT, BYTE, SHL, SHR and SAR ... run in the x86-64 and AArch64 models over 1,295,988 cases (chains 130, 57073, 1868, 8453).
clearedSpotChecks.note: Lockfile versions checked independently. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/65e803329acd2bfd6fca0b3ff2012f7c55aa1bdf/rust/Cargo.lock pins ruint 1.20.0, revm-interpreter 43.0.2 and revm-bytecode 43.0.0. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/v1.5.6/Cargo.lock pins ruint 1.19.0, revm-interpreter 42.0.0 and revm-bytecode 42.0.0. Neither is the withdrawn ruint 1.21.0. web3_clientVersion returned op-reth/v2.10.0-rc.4-65e80332/x86_64-linux on mainnet.unichain.org, rpc-gel.inkonchain.com and rpc.soneium.org, and reth/v2.5.2-9e380dd/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/base/v1.5.6 on mainnet.base.org. I ran my own vector set by eth_call with a code override: 640 cases per seed (seeds 11 and 12) of DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, ADDMOD, MULMOD, EXP, SIGNEXTEND, LT, GT, SLT, SGT, BYTE, SHL, SHR and SAR on edge operands, with half of the MULMOD cases built in the ruint 1.21.0 fault shape (top 128 bits of the modulus equal to the high half of the product) or modulus 2^256-1, as FullMath.sol:24 uses. Unichain, Base and Soneium returned 0 mismatches against Python integers in 3,840 cases. The words read by FullMath.sol:24 and TickMath.sol:61-63 come from these opcodes. The binary lift itself was not repeated.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 4, run live. Nested-frame sequences over the PoolManager's transient and persistent slot shapes on chains 10, 8453, 130, 7777777, 480, 57073, 1868: a reverted or halted frame restored previous transient and persistent values, a nested revert was not undone twice, and TSTORE under STATICCALL failed.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I wrote an independent sequence and ran it by eth_call with state overrides on all seven endpoints. The outer frame sets transient IS_UNLOCKED_SLOT (Lock.sol:8) to 1 and a keccak-shaped persistent slot to 1; a DELEGATECALL callee writes both slots and a second transient slot and REVERTs; a second callee writes the transient slot and STOPs; a STATICCALL callee attempts TSTORE; a fourth callee writes the second transient slot, DELEGATECALLs a fifth that writes the transient and persistent slots and returns, then hits INVALID. Every endpoint (op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 on Unichain, Ink and Soneium; Base v1.5.6; op-reth on OP Mainnet; conduit-op-reth on Zora; world-chain on World Chain) returned [1,1,0,0,3,1,0,3,3,0,1,0], which is the specified result: reverted writes undone, the inner successful frame undone with its reverting parent, the static TSTORE refused. This is the shape CurrencyDelta.sol:35-39 depends on. eth_call runs one transaction, so clearing of transient storage between transactions of a block was not tested here.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 3. Legacy jump destination analysis located in each binary and run in the models; reth's execution cache keyed by the full 32-byte code hash, so two codes cannot share an analysis.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I ran seven jump programs by eth_call on Unichain, Base and Soneium: a jump to a real JUMPDEST succeeds; a jump to a 0x5b byte inside PUSH1 data fails with InvalidJump; JUMPI with condition 2^255 takes the jump (the whole word is tested); a destination with bit 64 set fails; a 0x5b inside a truncated PUSH11 at the end of code fails; a jump to the code length fails; JUMPI with condition 0 falls through. All seven matched the specification on all three endpoints. The cache claim rests on the cited reth and fixed-cache source files in the work directory, which I did not re-fetch; the live answers give no sign of a shared analysis.
